correctness.rationale: Reconstructed all 21 arcs and exhaustively enumerated all nonempty directed-acyclic indegree<=1/outdegree<=1 arc subsets: 2,940 faces f=(21,168,630,1113,819,189), mod2 ordinary boundary ranks (20,148,482,616,165). Independently rebuilt source-specified 1,424 toggle Morse pairs and topologically sorted the 2,940-vertex reversed matched-incidence Hasse graph, giving critical cells {0:1,3:22,4:45,5:24}. Independently computed the exact integer 22x45 Morse differential and Smith factors (seven units; all other zero), verified critical ∂5=0. Thus free integral reduced Betti 15,38,24 but this alone would not imply wedge. Reconstructed 15 independent mod2 H^3 cocycles modulo full 482-rank coboundaries and calculated their cup-one squares on all 5-simplices; all lie in the 165-rank degree-5 coboundary image. Consequently Sq²:H³->H⁵ is zero. After canceling seven 3/4 unit cellular pairs, 5-cell attachments to wedge^15 S3 vee wedge^38 S4 have classes in (Z/2)^15 + Z^38; ∂5 kills free parts, Sq² detects each mod2 Hopf part. Thus all attachments nullhomotopic. This proves the full wedge rather than only homology.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge new full integral homotopy calculation for the *nontransitive* doubly regular Paley-7 tournament. Caputi–Collari–Di Trani–Smith 2024 full postprint explicitly treats transitive tournaments (Theorem 5.1), linear graphs, polygons and small grids, with general module decomposition not resolving this irreducible target. The earlier Caputi et al. definitions do not state a Paley seven calculation. The closest Resultary Paley tournament results compute directed *flag* complexes at 19/31 vertices, a different construction. Need distinguish a general theorem that some transitive multipath complexes are wedges from this specific 15/38/24 integral wedge and Hopf Sq² obstruction.
